The argument correctly identifies that holes must be placed at king‑distance ≥ 2, giving an independence density of at most \(1/4\) among all unit squares. Translating this to the ratio of holes to occupied squares yields the upper bound \(h_n\le n/3\). The constructive family of polyominoes (a full \(2m\times2m\) square with interior even‑coordinate cells removed) attains a hole‑to‑square ratio arbitrarily close to \(1/3\), and satisfies all connectivity and boundary‑disjointness requirements. Hence the limit \(\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{h_n}{n}=1/3\) is indeed correct.
